hearty

HAR-tee -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, HAR. Careful: it sounds close to 'hardy,' a different word. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Hearty is loudly vigorous and cheerful.

Grandpa's hearty singing carried over the whole campfire.

Example

The coach does not just say congratulations. His hearty 'WELL DONE!' booms across the gym, his handshake rattles your arm, and his laugh arrives before the door finishes opening.

Everything about the coach is hearty: loudly vigorous and cheerful, with real force behind the warmth. Hearty describes cheer with muscle in it -- booming greetings, roaring cheers, back-slapping congratulations.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

vigorous: Vigorous means full of strength, energy, and effort -- a vigorous workout, a vigorous scrubbing -- and it carries no cheer at all. Hearty keeps the energy but aims it at warmth: a hearty greeting is friendliness delivered at full strength.

genial: Genial means pleasantly friendly in a mild, easygoing way -- a genial host smiles, chats, and keeps things comfortable. Hearty is friendliness with force behind it: the genial host offers a warm hello, while the hearty one booms it across the room and shakes your whole arm.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

faint: weak and barely noticeable

glum: silent and gloomy in mood

Where it sits · how much force joins the cheerfulness

jolly → hearty → boisterous

jolly vs. hearty: Jolly covers the cheerful half only -- a jolly mood can be quiet -- while hearty adds volume and force: a hearty welcome arrives at full strength.

boisterous vs. hearty: Boisterous goes a step past hearty: a hearty welcome is warm force aimed at making someone glad, while boisterous is noise and energy running loose -- rowdy, thumping, and hard to settle down.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — heart: the heart (Old English heorte)

suffix — -y: full of (Old English -ig)

Put it together: Hearty is literally 'full of heart' -- cheer and strength pumped straight from the chest, which is why hearty laughs, cheers, and welcomes all come out at full volume.

Use the root in a new word: hearten: Her reply, when it finally came, heartened him more than he let on.

Root Check

Word Choice

Hearty describes cheer delivered with force: a hearty laugh, welcome, cheer, or handshake. Two traps to know: hearty also describes filling food (a hearty stew), a separate everyday sense; and do not confuse hearty with hardy, which means tough enough to survive -- a hardy plant, but a hearty greeting.
